predecessors.name: Sagaing Kingdom
predecessors.text: Sagaing, Thado Minbya's kingdom, which 'declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava'

successors.name: Shan States
successors.text: Ava and Upper Burma, taken by the Confederation of Shan States in March 1527

successors.name: Toungoo Empire
successors.text: Toungoo, Kyaukse and Taungdwingyi: the 202 cells that Cliopatria's Toungoo row takes from Ava in 1502

ledger.x: 26 February 1365: Thado Minbya founds the Kingdom of Ava.
December 1385: the Forty Years' War begins.
1408: Pegu drives Ava out of Arakan.
1415: Minye Kyawswa conquers the Irrawaddy delta.
March 1415: Minye Kyawswa is killed and the delta lost.
Early 1424: the war ends in stalemate.
1502: Ava's king gives Toungoo's governor Kyaukse.
March 1527: the Confederation of Shan States takes Ava.
March 1527: the Burmese kingdom of Ava ends.

wars.name: Forty Years' War
wars.outcome: Stalemate: 'preserving the independence of Hanthawaddy, and effectively ending Ava's efforts to rebuild the erstwhile Pagan Kingdom'; Ava held Kale, Mohnyin and Launggyet in 1404-1406 and the delta in 1415.

wars.name: Confederation of Shan States' conquest of Ava
wars.outcome: 'In March 1525, the combined armies of Confederation and Prome sacked the city of Ava' and 'On 25 March 1527, the Confederation forces captured Ava' (Prome page); Ava was 'under intensified Shan raids for the first quarter of the 16th century'.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a surveyed frontier: the Shan, Arakan Yoma and southern (Prome, Pegu) edges are approximate, and the Toungoo and Shan vassal margins are claims.
